title: Write features/daw/sidecar_formats.feature and features/daw/STEPS.md (red)
description:
## Intent
Write the behavior before the code: the three M1 stories as a feature file and the step vocabulary.

## Scope
- `features/daw/sidecar_formats.feature`: every scenario of the M1 stories (round trip, reading the DAW's own sidecars, malformed sidecars), `.asd` round-trip rows tagged `@asd-write` and skipped by the runner if M0 said no-go.
- `features/daw/STEPS.md`: normative step vocabulary in the house style of `features/sources/STEPS.md` (State / Given / When / Then tables; tests never touch the network; a fresh temp dir per scenario).
- Step definitions in `crates/apricity-daw/tests/conformance.rs`, all failing (no implementation yet).

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-daw --test conformance` fails on every new scenario for the right reason (paste the summary line).

Commit: part of the first `feat` commit of the implementing task (specs land with the code that makes them green).

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
